reach.rationale: Only long-stable APIs (App Router conventions, Metadata, route segment config, next/navigation useRouter); zero experimental, preview or recently-stable surface.

evidence: app/lib/api.ts:11-43 — all API access centralized behind one module, nothing leaked into components

evidence: app/app/page.tsx:6 — revalidate=0/force-dynamic matches SPEC.md's request-time live-data requirement
app/lib/api.ts:11-18 — runtime in-memory caching is the explicitly permitted strategy
justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used, so none are unjustified; the stable choices made (dynamic rendering, no-store) directly serve the spec's live-API requirement.

findings.issue: Triple-redundant dynamic opt-out (dynamic='force-dynamic', revalidate=0, fetchCache='force-no-store') repeated across ~8 route files, on top of per-fetch cache:'no-store' (app/lib/api.ts:28)
findings.suggestion: Keep one mechanism (e.g. force-dynamic on the root layout only); these exported constants are exactly what a future Cache Components migration would have to delete from every route (removed under cacheComponents per v16.0.0 route-segment-config version history)

summary: The app is built entirely on long-stable, fully supported Next.js APIs and touches nothing experimental, preview or canary — no cacheComponents/use cache, no PPR, no proxy.ts, no experimental hooks. Its only noteworthy trait is heavy, redundant use of the legacy dynamic-rendering segment configs, which are stable today but slated for removal once Cache Components is adopted. Risk of breaking-change exposure is essentially zero.
